4. Mr AY Ahmed Ali, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the impugned order as passed by the respondent No. 3 cannot be deemed to be a decree under the Act and that the jurisdiction of the civil Court is not ousted either clearly or by necessary implication. Referring to section 45 of the Act, he submits that the insured died of Asthma within 3 months of the issue of the policy but in the medical report there is no mention that he was suffering from any such serious disease. The insured obtained the policy by suppressing the material facts in collusion with the officers of the appellant. In the facts, the appellant is entitled to institute the suit. 

 7. Mr Ahmed Ali tried to submit that there being no Claims Settlement Board constituted under section 47C(2) of the Act by the Government, the decision of the learned Subordinate Judge treating the order of the respondent No. 3 as final and the effect of decree is also erroneous. We find that the impugned order was passed on consideration of section 47J of the Act. 

 Section 47A of the Act deals specifically for settlement of the dispute if any with regard to life policy Section says that if the dispute arising under a policy of life insurance assuring a sum not exceeding five thousand Taka may be referred to the Controller of Insurance and the Controller may, after hearing the parties and taking such evidence as he may, in his absolute discretion, consider necessary, settle the dispute Under sub-section (2) of section 47A, the decision of the Controller of Insurance is final and shall not be called in question in any court and shall be deemed to be a decree of a Court. There is of course no other provision in the Act providing any forum for settlement of any claim in respect of a life insurance policy exceeding taka five thousand.
